engine_name: MLC-LLM (Apache TVM / ML Compilation), nightly 0.20.dev (2026), MLCEngine inference engine
cuda_128_compatible: Yes. MLC-LLM ships a prebuilt nightly wheel for CUDA 12.8 — no source build required for the runtime. Install with: pip install --pre -U -f https://mlc.ai/wheels mlc-llm-nightly-cu128 mlc-ai-nightly-cu128. This installs both the MLC-LLM package and the matching TVM/mlc-ai backend compiled for CUDA 12.8. Other prebuilt variants exist (cu130, rocm61, rocm62, cpu). The A6000 (sm_86) is auto-detected correctly by TVM target detection ('arch': 'sm_86', max_shared_memory_per_block 49152), so the runtime side needs no manual build. IMPORTANT caveat: while the runtime wheel is prebuilt, running any NEW model architecture (or a model with no published .so) requires compiling a model library with `mlc_llm compile`, which invokes TVM kernel autotuning specific to sm_86 and can take a long time (often reported in the tens of minutes to hours for large models). Python 3.13 is the recommended environment for the nightly wheels.
gemma4_support: NO — google/gemma-4-31B-it is NOT supported as of mid-2026. GitHub issue #3477 ([Model Request] Support Gemma4, filed 2026-04-05) documents that the nightly build detects the architecture string 'gemma4' but it is not registered in the supported model list, producing 'ValueError: Unknown model type: gemma4'. The issue is OPEN and UNADDRESSED (no maintainer response, no PR). The commit history on main through 2026-05-11 contains NO Gemma 4 work. Three architectural blockers are documented: (1) multimodal weight nesting (language model weights live under model.language_model.*, plus audio_tower/vision_tower components that current Gemma loaders do not expect; config uses Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration); (2) config fields (query_pre_attn_scalar, head_dim) are nested in text_config rather than at root, causing Typeerror with the gemma2/gemma3 templates; (3) the 'gemma4' model type is simply unregistered. Required format is MLC's own compiled format (mlc-chat-config.json + params_shard_*.bin + a per-target .so model library), produced via convert_weight + gen_config + compile. The official mlc-ai HuggingFace org only publishes up to Gemma 3 (e.g. gemma-3-27b-it-q4f16_1-MLC, gemma-3-4b-it-q4bf16_0-MLC). For Gemma 4, only a community-contributed welcoma/gemma-4-E2B-it-q4f16_1-MLC (WebGPU/wasm, the tiny E2B variant) exists — there is NO Gemma 4 31B MLC artifact, official or community. [uncertain] Gemma 3 itself has had stability problems on MLC (issue #3206: NaN probability-distribution crashes even with official precompiled 4b/12b weights), which raises concern that even if Gemma 4 31B were added, dense-model numerical stability is not guaranteed.
per_request_reasoning_toggle: NO documented per-request reasoning toggle. MLC-LLM has no equivalent of vLLM's chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking exposed on the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. For R1-style/Qwen3 thinking models the approach is build-time: select a conversation template (e.g. --conv-template deepseek_r1_qwen) at gen_config time, and a recent commit (#3484, 2026-04-20) only 'strips reasoning in history for Qwen3 chat' — i.e. it post-processes thinking out of conversation history rather than letting a client toggle thinking per request. There is no Gemma-4-specific reasoning parser, and since Gemma 4 itself is unsupported, no per-request thinking control for Gemma 4 exists. [uncertain] Whether the OpenAI server passes arbitrary chat_template_kwargs through to the template at runtime is undocumented; community reports indicate it does not provide reliable per-request thinking control.
per_request_reasoning_budget: NO. There is no per-request reasoning/thinking token budget parameter in MLC-LLM (no thinking_budget_tokens or equivalent). Reasoning length can only be bounded indirectly via max_tokens, which caps total generation rather than the reasoning segment specifically. Since Gemma 4 is unsupported, this is doubly moot. [uncertain]
tool_calling_support: Tool/function calling IS exposed via the OpenAI-compatible REST API (tools / tool_choice fields, modeled on the OpenAI spec), but reliability is poor and model-dependent. There is no Gemma-4-specific tool-call parser (vLLM's dedicated 'gemma4' parser has no MLC analogue). Documented failure modes: issue #3344 — Qwen3 models (Qwen3-8B/14B-MLC) cannot recognize tools at all when following the official function-calling docs; WebLLM issue #712 — most tool-capable models return an empty array [] and only Hermes-2-Pro-Mistral works, and even that model ignores tool_choice (emits tool calls even when tool_choice='none'). Tool calling for an unsupported architecture like Gemma 4 31B would require it to first be added AND for a working chat template + parser to be wired up, neither of which exists. Streaming partial tool-call assembly is a known fragile area across local engines generally.
openai_api_compatible: Yes. `mlc_llm serve` launches an OpenAI-compatible REST server (default http://127.0.0.1:8000, configurable --host/--port) exposing /v1/chat/completions with SSE streaming, plus Python MLCEngine / AsyncMLCEngine clients mirroring the OpenAI interface. It advertises 'complete OpenAI API support' including function calling and JSON mode. Works with openai-python / httpx asyncio clients. [uncertain] Some advanced fields (e.g. reasoning_content separation, chat_template_kwargs passthrough) are less mature than vLLM/SGLang; community requests note gaps in parsing thinking output into a separate reasoning property.
continuous_batching: Yes. MLCEngine performs continuous batching of concurrent requests (it is positioned as a high-performance serving engine, not just single-stream). For the target load (<=10 concurrent users, 4-8 parallel sub-agents) this is adequate in principle. [uncertain] Real-world batching throughput for a dense 31B at int4 on a single A6000 has not been benchmarked here, and is irrelevant until Gemma 4 is supported.
installation_steps:
Runtime (host-native, CUDA 12.8, Ubuntu/Debian RunPod, no Docker):
1. Create a Python 3.13 env (conda recommended): conda create -n mlc python=3.13 -y && conda activate mlc
2. Install prebuilt nightly wheel + TVM backend for CUDA 12.8:
   python -m pip install --pre -U -f https://mlc.ai/wheels mlc-llm-nightly-cu128 mlc-ai-nightly-cu128
3. Verify: python -c "import mlc_llm; print(mlc_llm.__version__)" and mlc_llm chat -h
For a model NOT yet packaged (which currently includes ALL Gemma 4 variants), you must additionally build a model library from source-converted weights (see serve_command) — this is the operationally heavy path and, for Gemma 4, is BLOCKED until issue #3477 is resolved (the architecture must first be added to the mlc-llm Python source, requiring a from-source build of mlc-llm rather than the wheel).
serve_command:
Not currently achievable for google/gemma-4-31B-it — the architecture is unregistered (ValueError: Unknown model type: gemma4). The intended workflow once a model is supported would be:
# 1. Generate config + process tokenizer
mlc_llm gen_config ./models/gemma-4-31B-it --quantization q4f16_1 --conv-template gemma_instruction -o ./dist/gemma-4-31B-it-q4f16_1-MLC --context-window-size 16384
# 2. Quantize/convert weights (CPU/GPU, minutes)
mlc_llm convert_weight ./models/gemma-4-31B-it --quantization q4f16_1 -o ./dist/gemma-4-31B-it-q4f16_1-MLC
# 3. Compile a CUDA sm_86 model library (TVM autotuning — long)
mlc_llm compile ./dist/gemma-4-31B-it-q4f16_1-MLC/mlc-chat-config.json --device cuda -o ./dist/gemma-4-31B-it-q4f16_1-cuda.so
# 4. Serve OpenAI API
mlc_llm serve ./dist/gemma-4-31B-it-q4f16_1-MLC --model-lib ./dist/gemma-4-31B-it-q4f16_1-cuda.so --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --mode interactive --overrides "context_window_size=16384;gpu_memory_utilization=0.88;tensor_parallel_shards=1"
Note: there is no working reasoning-toggle or gemma4 tool parser flag to add here. [uncertain] exact conv-template name for Gemma 4 does not exist yet.
speculative_decoding: MLC-LLM has historically had limited/experimental speculative decoding support (Eagle/medusa-style and small-draft modes have appeared in the codebase), but it is NOT a turnkey, well-documented feature on the OpenAI server. There is NO support for Gemma 4's MTP draft (mtp-gemma-4-31B-it.gguf) — MLC does not consume GGUF draft models (it uses its own compiled .so libraries), and both base and draft would each need to be added/compiled. Expected speedup is therefore not estimable for this engine/model combination. [uncertain]
known_issues_gemma4: 1. Gemma 4 entirely unsupported: issue #3477 'Unknown model type: gemma4', OPEN/unaddressed (filed 2026-04-05), no maintainer response, not in any commit through 2026-05-11. Blockers: multimodal weight nesting (model.language_model.*, vision_tower/audio_tower), nested text_config fields (query_pre_attn_scalar, head_dim), unregistered model type. 2. WebLLM issue #810 requests Gemma 4 with same gap. 3. Gemma 3 precedent of instability: issue #3206 — NaN probability-distribution InternalError crashes Gemma 3 4b/12b even with official MLC precompiled weights (1b worked), suggesting risk for dense Gemma models. 4. Issue #3382 (2025-11-22) raised 'is this project abandoned?' citing slow addition of new architectures (Qwen3, Gemma 3, Granite 4) — the repo IS still committing (TVM-runtime refactors, Qwen3 fixes through May 2026) but new-model throughput is slow (286 open issues, 29 open PRs). 5. Function calling broken for recent models (#3344 Qwen3, #712 WebLLM empty tool_calls).
vram_usage: Estimated ~17-20 GB for a dense 31B at 4-bit (q4f16_1) weights, plus KV cache for 16k context. With f16 KV cache a dense ~31B model at 16k context typically needs roughly 4-8 GB of KV, giving a rough total of ~22-28 GB on the A6000 48GB, leaving comfortable headroom for the bge-small-en-v1.5 embedder (~0.13 GB) and bge-reranker-v2-m3 (~2.3 GB) co-resident. MLC's gpu_memory_utilization override (e.g. 0.88) pre-allocates a KV pool, so co-residency would require tuning that down. [uncertain] — no measured numbers for Gemma 4 31B on MLC exist because the model cannot be loaded; these are extrapolated from comparable 27-32B int4 deployments.
small_scale_fit: Poor fit for this specific deployment right now. The runtime install is clean (prebuilt cu128 wheel), but MLC's value proposition (cross-platform compiled kernels) comes with high operational overhead: every unsupported model requires a from-source mlc-llm build to add the architecture, then convert_weight + gen_config + TVM compile (autotuning, potentially hours, and re-run whenever you change context length, quantization, or move to different hardware/another A6000). Compared to the llama.cpp baseline (GGUF drop-in, --jinja chat template, no per-target compile) or SGLang (HF safetensors load, mature reasoning/tool parsers), MLC adds compile/maintenance burden without compensating benefit at this scale. The unresolved Gemma 4 support is the decisive blocker.
overall_recommendation: NOT_VIABLE (for google/gemma-4-31B-it as of mid-2026). Decisive reason: Gemma 4 is not supported (issue #3477 open and unaddressed, no commits referencing gemma4 through 2026-05-11, no Gemma 4 31B MLC artifact). Even setting that aside, MLC lacks per-request reasoning toggle and per-request reasoning budget, has no Gemma-4 tool-call parser, has documented unreliable tool calling on recent models (#3344, #712), and a Gemma 3 NaN-crash precedent (#3206). PROS: clean prebuilt CUDA 12.8 wheel; native sm_86/A6000 detection; OpenAI-compatible server with streaming; continuous batching; once compiled, kernels are fast and portable across platforms; repo is still actively maintained (TVM-runtime refactors, Qwen3 fixes May 2026). CONS: target model unsupported with multiple architectural blockers; adding a new architecture requires a from-source build plus hours-long per-target TVM compilation; no per-request reasoning control or budget; weak/unreliable tool calling; slow new-model throughput (286 open issues, 29 open PRs); reasoning handled only via build-time conv-template + history stripping. Recommendation: do NOT choose MLC-LLM for this Gemma 4 31B deployment. Prefer vLLM (dedicated gemma4 parser/reasoning), or llama.cpp/SGLang as the simpler baselines. Reconsider MLC only if/when issue #3477 lands a registered gemma4 architecture AND per-request reasoning control is added.
